title: O Thou, at Whose Divine Command
description: O Thou, at Whose Divine Command in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Alford wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 486, “The Seed of the Word”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou, at whose di-vine com-mand Good seed is sown in ev-ery land, Thy ho-ly spir-it now im-part, And for Thy word pre-pare each heart!

lines: O Thou, at whose divine command
Good seed is sown in every land,
And for Thy word prepare each heart!
Not 'mid the thorns of worldly thought,
Nor soon by passing plunderers caught,
Nor lacking depth the root to feed,
May we receive Thy spirit's seed;
But may it, where Thy sowers toil,
Fall in a good and honest soil;
And springing up from firmest root,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Henry Alford died in 1871.
credits: Words by Henry Alford (1810–1871), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
